adjuster_notes: Heavy rain overnight. Basement floor drain backed up and flooded the basement with wastewater. The basement is unfinished, used only for storage and utilities - never finished as living space. Sump pump was inspected the same day and found in proper working order, no mechanical failure. No creek, river or other body of water near the property overflowed.
why: Sewer/drain backup, not flood - HO-2026-01 covers it, sump pump condition satisfies the endorsement's own condition. Straightforward once the endorsement's $500 deductible is looked up.

adjuster_notes: Regional flooding after three days of storms. The creek behind the property overflowed its banks and backed up through the basement floor drain and sewer connection. Policyholder holds the water backup endorsement (HO-2026-01) and is asking why that doesn't apply here.
why: Dependent case named in the task sheet: the notes reveal the water's origin is flood (creek overflow), which HO-2026-01 explicitly does NOT restore even when the water enters through a drain. Reading only the claim record (not the notes) or stopping at 'has HO-2026-01' without checking the endorsement's own flood carve-out gets this wrong.

adjuster_notes: HVAC compressor failed suddenly and stopped cooling. Unit is 2 years old. Policyholder confirms the manufacturer's warranty is a 5-year parts-and-labor warranty and the manufacturer has already agreed to send a technician under that warranty at no cost.
why: Dependent: HO-2026-03 excludes equipment still covered by a manufacturer's warranty 'to the extent that warranty responds' - and the notes say the manufacturer already agreed to cover it. Skipping the notes and only checking 'is this a covered breakdown' gets this wrong.

adjuster_notes: Refrigerator (12 years old) stopped running after a power surge from a lightning strike on the neighborhood transformer, off the residence premises. No manufacturer warranty in force. Failed compressor retained for inspection.
why: Power surge originating off-premises is a covered breakdown cause under HO-2026-03; no warranty conflict. Deductible is the endorsement's $500, not the base $1,000.

policy_form: HO-3-2026 (base form only, no equipment endorsement)
adjuster_notes: Furnace output has been declining for months. Technician found long-term internal corrosion and rust on the heat exchanger, with no single sudden event reported by the homeowner.
why: Dependent: the notes describe gradual deterioration and rust, not a sudden event - base exclusion 10 (wear and tear, rust) applies, and there is no equipment breakdown endorsement on this policy to add it back. A reader who only sees 'furnace stopped working' without the notes might assume this is a routine breakdown claim.

adjuster_notes: Underground water supply line between the street and the house cracked and leaked, undermining a section of the driveway. No third-party excavation involved; line failed from age.
why: Straightforward service line failure under HO-2026-02, endorsement deductible $500 replaces the base $1,000.

adjuster_notes: House fire started in the attic and destroyed the roof structure and surfacing. Cause of loss confirmed as fire by the fire department report, not wind or hail. Claimed amount of $120,000 already reflects the adjuster's replacement-cost estimate for the roof and attic.
why: Dependent: HO-2026-08 restricts settlement to ACV only for wind/hail losses to roof surfacing; fire losses stay on the base form's replacement-cost basis. An agent that sees 'HO-2026-08 attached' and reaches for ACV without checking the notes for cause of loss would wrongly apply depreciation here. Deductible is the base $1,000, since HO-2026-08 doesn't carry its own deductible.

adjuster_notes: Policyholder's identity was used to open a fraudulent credit line. Out-of-pocket costs of $1,800 for credit monitoring, notarized affidavits and lost wages attending resolution meetings, documented by receipts.
why: Straightforward identity fraud claim, endorsement deductible $250.

adjuster_notes: Detached shed destroyed by fire. Investigation, including the insured's own statement, established the insured set the fire deliberately to collect insurance proceeds. Local fire marshal's report supports arson by the insured.
why: Base exclusion 8, intentional loss by an insured. No endorsement can restore this; a plain exclusion lookup is enough.

adjuster_notes: Engagement ring, scheduled on the policy at an agreed value of $8,000, stolen from the home during a break-in. Police report filed same day.
why: Dependent: the base form's $2,000 special limit on jewelry theft does not apply once the item is scheduled under HO-2026-04, which also carries no deductible. An agent that applies the base form's jewelry sub-limit without noticing 'scheduled' in the notes would under-pay this by $6,000.
